samples.summary: Design doc records the wrong reuse for offline-copy recovery. `offline-local-persistence.md` states "we already have the machinery for it in `DocumentCopyService` / `POST /documents/:id/copy`" and its See Also says "document-copy.md — the copy engine the offline-copy recovery path reuses". The implementation reuses neither: `offline-copy-recovery.ts` calls `createWorkspaceDocument` + `applyImportedContent` (the *import* engine, `app/documents/apply-imported-content.ts`), and for notes it hand-rolls a live `Client`/`Document` attach-and-edit that goes through no shared engine at all. `POST /documents/:id/copy` is a server-side copy *from a live source document* (docs/design/document-copy.md:56-64), which cannot copy locally-archived bytes whose source may be deleted — so the implementation's choice is defensible, but the design doc points a future reader at the wrong subsystem and the wrong cross-reference.
samples.evidence: Doc: "we already have the machinery for it in `DocumentCopyService` / `POST /documents/:id/copy`"; "See Also — document-copy.md — the copy engine the offline-copy recovery path reuses". Code: offline-copy-recovery.ts imports `applyImportedContent` from `@/app/documents/apply-imported-content` and `createWorkspaceDocument` from `@/api/workspaces`; `writeNote()` constructs its own `new Client(...)`.

samples.summary: Design doc and implementation contradict each other on archive sweep scoping. The doc states: "The thirty-day sweep is deliberately **not** scoped to the signed-in user for live entries … **Archives stay scoped**: another account's is the only copy of work their SDK could not reconcile, and it is theirs to collect." The code does the opposite — `collectStale` calls `dropArchivesWhere(BY_ARCHIVED_AT, range)` with no user filter, its own comment argues the reverse of the doc ("Archives are swept on exactly the same terms … scoping the sweep to this user left another account's content with no collection path at all"), and a test asserts the cross-account behaviour (`wafflebase-doc-store-cleanup.test.ts`, "collects another account's stale entries and their stale archives"). One of the two is stale; the design doc is the canonical record and no longer describes what ships.
samples.evidence: `const archived = await this.dropArchivesWhere(BY_ARCHIVED_AT, range);` — the `onlyUser` parameter of `dropArchivesWhere` (line 1309) exists solely for this scoping and is passed by no caller.

samples.summary: The store-key parsing rule is duplicated three times, in a module whose own doc comment warns against exactly that. `wafflebase-doc-store.ts` exports `documentKeyOf` with the note "Defined here because this module is where store keys are consumed, and two copies of the rule is how the guard that matched a lock name against a store key came to be silently false." The new `offline-copy.ts` then defines a byte-identical private `documentIdOf`, and `offline-copy-recovery.ts:146` inlines the same two lines again. Both new modules already import from `wafflebase-doc-store`, so reuse was free. If the SDK's key shape ever changes, this is three places to find rather than one — the precise failure the exported helper was extracted to prevent.
samples.evidence: offline-copy.ts:52-55 `function documentIdOf(docKey){const parts=docKey.split("/");return parts[parts.length-1]||docKey;}` vs wafflebase-doc-store.ts:212-215 `export function documentKeyOf(key){const parts=key.split("/");return parts[parts.length-1]||key;}` vs offline-copy-recovery.ts:146-147.

samples.summary: `documentIdsIn` reinvents a workspace document listing that already exists in the same file. `api/workspaces.ts` already exports `fetchWorkspaceDocuments(workspaceId, folderId?)` (line 290), hitting `GET /workspaces/:id/documents`. The new helper instead adds a cross-module import of `fetchDocuments` from `./documents`, fetches *every* document the user can see across all workspaces, and filters client-side — plus a second `fetchWorkspace(ref)` round-trip purely to resolve slug→id, which `fetchWorkspaceDocuments` would not need. That is two extra requests on every workspace delete and every member removal, and a whole-account listing used to answer a per-workspace question. The existing helper lists only the workspace root (no folder recursion), which is a real reason it may not be a drop-in — but that constraint is not recorded anywhere, and the design doc's "folders included" phrasing is the only hint.
samples.evidence: `documentIdsIn` does `await fetchWorkspace(ref)` then `await fetchDocuments()` and filters on `document.workspaceId`, while `fetchWorkspaceDocuments` at line 290 of the same file already fetches `${BASE}/${seg(workspaceId)}/documents`.

samples.summary: As landed, none of the design's Goals are reachable by any user. `supportsClientKey()` gates both opt-in entry points on `@yorkie-js/react >= 0.7.23` (`MinClientKeyVersion`), and `packages/frontend/package.json:66` pins `0.7.22` — so the Settings section is not rendered, the chip's offer is suppressed, `useDurableDocument` refuses every document, and no edit is ever persisted. The design doc states this outcome deliberately ("PR 4 lands inert, and stays inert until one upstream release … the Goals at the top of this document are unmet until the dependency is bumped"), so this is design-conformant rather than a defect — but it is worth stating plainly that this change ships ~4,000 lines of storage, election, erase and recovery machinery whose user-facing behaviour is unexercisable on the pinned dependency, and that the only acceptance evidence available is unit tests that stub `supportsClientKey` to `true`.

`keepArchives` is a vestigial option from a superseded iteration of this very design. `WafflebaseDocStore.dropAllForUser` (line 1085) and `eraseOfflineData` (offline-erase.ts:29) both accept it, and the store's comment justifies it as "for the one caller that did not ask for any of this: a session the server expired". That caller no longer exists — the final design has the 401 arm erase *nothing at all* (`eraseLocalData: "none"`), so `eraseOfflineDataOnLogout` passes no options and nothing in the tree ever sets the flag. The option and its rationale document a code path the change deliberately removed.
samples.evidence: grep for `keepArchives` across packages/frontend/src returns only the two declarations and the two lines inside the store that read it; no call site passes it.
searchedFor: read the logout eraseLocalData arm in api/auth.ts

samples.summary: The change lands PRs 2–5 of its own Rollout table as a single diff, against the discipline the design doc states for itself: "The structural change and the behavior change land separately, so that a regression in either is unambiguous." This diff contains the store (PR 2), the per-document client and app lock (PR 3), the wiring plus Settings/chip opt-in, unload behaviour and offline-copy recovery (PR 4), and the `sync-status.md` revision (PR 5) at once. The stated benefit of the split — attributing a regression to either the structure or the behaviour — is forfeited. Noted as fit-with-plan rather than a defect in the code; a reviewer cannot retroactively split a submitted branch, but the doc's Rollout section should either be honoured or amended to describe what actually shipped.
samples.evidence: Rollout table rows 2–5 all appear in this one diff: wafflebase-doc-store.ts, durable-session.ts/use-durable-document.ts, durable-yorkie-provider.tsx + settings/page.tsx + sync-status-chip.tsx, and the sync-status.md edits.

samples.summary: `applyBoardElements` gains behaviour that changes the existing Miro import path, and the design doc does not record it. `MappedInit` now falls back to `id` when `__id` is absent (`handleOf`), and `mapDescendants` recursively registers every group child's id into the handle map. Both are needed by the new offline-recovery reader, but they also alter how *Miro-imported* boards resolve connector endpoints — a mapped element that happens to carry an `id`, or a group whose children share ids with a handle, now resolves where it previously did not. `offline-local-persistence.md` describes recovery as requiring "no SDK change at all" and says nothing about modifying the import engine, so a future reader of either document has no record that the import path was touched on behalf of offline persistence.
samples.evidence: `function handleOf(element){return element.__id ?? element.id;}` and the new `mapDescendants` recursion, both reached unconditionally from `applyBoardElements`'s pass 1 — the same function Miro import calls.

samples.summary: Unrelated whole-file reformatting inflates the diff. `packages/frontend/src/lib/utils.ts`, `packages/frontend/vite.config.ts` and `packages/frontend/src/components/__tests__/collab-document-provider.test.tsx` are churned from double to single quotes (and semicolon additions) with no relation to offline persistence — the test file in particular is ~60 lines of pure quote flipping around two substantive mock additions. Prettier is write-only in this repo and no lane checks formatting, so this is reviewer cost with no enforcement benefit, and it obscures the two real changes in that test file.
samples.evidence: `-import { render } from "@testing-library/react";` / `+import { render } from '@testing-library/react';` repeated throughout, alongside the two real additions (the `YorkieProvider` pass-through and the `@tanstack/react-query` mock).
